comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Implemented as Gerrit change 2256 —
https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2256 (commit 259a645961fc, branch
`e668-mutation-sandbox`). Not closing until Verified +1 AND merged.

## What landed

- **`scripts/mutation_sandbox.py`** (144 LOC) — mechanism probe, Seatbelt profile
  generation, `bwrap` argv construction, fail-closed `wrap()`, and `sandbox_env()`.
- **`scripts/mutation_gate.py`** — both shard-test-executing subprocesses in
  `execute_shard` wrapped: the baseline `pytest` and the `mutmut run` mutant test-run.
  778 LOC, under the 800 cap, which is why the logic lives in its own module.
- **`tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py`** — 14 tests.
- **`docs/local-dev-env.md`** — operator note on `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED`.

## The mutation check found a real gap in my own tests

After wiring, I seeded two defects to check the tests had teeth:

1. Removing `--max-children 1` → the existing concurrency assertion went RED. Good.
2. **Removing the sandbox wrap from the `mutmut run` call → all 42 tests stayed
   GREEN.** The enforcement tests proved the *module* denies, but nothing bound it to
   the call site, so deleting the control was invisible.

That is the AC this ticket wrote and my first cut did not satisfy. Closed it with
three call-site-binding tests (`test_the_mutmut_run_subprocess_is_sandbox_wrapped`
and siblings). Re-seeding defect 2 now fails with a message naming the incident.

## Enforcement is observed, not asserted

The live tests execute under the sandbox and check the filesystem afterward rather
than inspecting argv — argv assertions would pass against a sandbox that denies
nothing. Measured on macOS 26.5.2: write outside the allow-list denied and file
absent; write inside succeeded; `rm -rf <protected>/*` denied with the target
surviving. They skip where no mechanism exists, so Linux `bwrap` enforcement remains
unverified until the ubuntu CI leg is green — the asymmetry this ticket's ACs state.

## Collateral fix

`tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py`'s `mutmut_run_concurrency` helper required
`_run`'s first argument to be a literal `ast.Tuple`; the wrapper made it a `Call`, so
its `--max-children` assertion silently matched nothing. Taught it to look through
the wrap — verified still RED when `--max-children` is removed, so the assertion kept
its strength rather than being loosened.

## Verification

`make lint` 0, `make typecheck` 0, complexity ratchet 0, 56 tests pass across the
sandbox and existing harness suites.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Change 2256 MERGED as `a26a73277c8a` (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1), submitted 18:22:36Z.

NOT closing on the strength of the merge. This ticket carries 11 acceptance criteria and all 11
are still unchecked; a merged change is evidence the code landed, not evidence each criterion is
satisfied. Earlier today I ticked a criterion on a file EXISTING rather than on it CONTAINING
what the criterion asked for, and the completion verifier correctly refused that close — so each
criterion here is being verified against the merged code with cited evidence before any box is
ticked.

The criterion I expect to be the real test is AC3: it explicitly rejects asserting on the
constructed wrapper argv and requires the test to OBSERVE enforcement — a probe that writes
outside the allow-list must exit non-zero with the file absent afterward. A suite that only
checks the command string would satisfy the letter of "a sandbox test exists" while leaving the
incident's actual failure mode untested. AC6 is the other one worth scrutiny: the Linux
write-deny has to be proven ON Linux in the ubuntu-latest CI leg, not inferred from the macOS
result, and a test that silently skips on the runner would not meet it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## AC verification against merged `a26a73277c8a`: 5 MET, 4 PARTIAL, 1 NOT MET

Verified each criterion against the merged code rather than ticking on the merge. Read-only; no
`mutmut run` executed.

**Genuinely delivered (MET).** AC3 is the important one and it holds properly: the enforcement
tests RUN a probe and assert on filesystem state afterward (`test_mutation_sandbox.py:71-79`
outside-deny asserting `not target.exists()`, `:83-92` inside-succeeds, `:96-108` reproducing the
incident's own `rm -rf <protected>/*` shape). The argv-only tests are separately quarantined at
`:264-301` and correctly labelled as binding checks. On this macOS host all 28 tests passed with
ZERO skips — real Seatbelt enforcement observed on a laptop. AC4, AC5 (no `unshare` fallback
anywhere — confirmed by repo-wide grep), AC7, AC9 and AC10 also hold.

**AC6 — NOT MET, and this is the one that matters.** The Linux write-deny is not proven on Linux.
`_build-and-test.yml:356-361` does install bubblewrap, but the merged code's OWN comment
(`mutation_sandbox.py:113-115`) records that GitHub's ubuntu runners ship bwrap while denying
unprivileged user namespaces (`bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied`), so the functional
probe correctly reports no mechanism. `probe()` returns `None`, the `@live` skipif at
`test_mutation_sandbox.py:61-64` fires, and all four enforcement tests SKIP on ubuntu-latest —
silently under `-q`. So `Verified +1` does not distinguish 'ran' from 'skipped', which is exactly
what this criterion was written to prevent. Two commits also contradict each other here:
`b63cf799ed90` installed bwrap specifically so these would not skip, and `a26a73277c8a` documents
that they still find no mechanism.

**AC1 and AC8 — PARTIAL, and I am NOT going to quietly reword them.** The implementation added a
`CI` branch (`mutation_sandbox.py:192-202`) that waives the sandbox entirely when no mechanism
exists on a CI runner, with a reasoned WARNING: a CI runner is already the disposable environment
the sandbox substitutes for, and the requirement exists to protect WORKSTATIONS. I think that
reasoning is sound, and it matters that the incident this ticket exists for happened on a
WORKSTATION — where this path still aborts or sandboxes. But the ACs as WRITTEN say the run
aborts when no mechanism is available, full stop, and they no longer describe the code. AC1 also
names the venv in the allow-list while `mutation_gate.py:594-596` deliberately excludes it
(`docs/local-dev-env.md:130` still says otherwise — doc/code drift).

**AC2 and AC11 — PARTIAL.** AC2's deny is tripped against a `mutmut run` argv SHAPE, not a real
mutmut invocation; the real call site is bound only by AST inspection. AC11's runtime half holds
(`sandbox_env` is applied to both subprocesses at `mutation_gate.py:597`) but the only test
asserts the RETURNED MAPPING, never a child's actual `HOME`, and `sandbox_env` has no call-site
binding test — deleting `mutation_gate.py:597` leaves the whole suite green. That is the same
defect class the author explicitly guarded `wrap` against.

Not closing. Splitting the residue into follow-ups so the delivered work is not held hostage to
it, per the operator's standing allowance to split as long as the work stays tracked.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## CORRECTION — I was about to discharge unmet criteria by filing tickets and closing anyway

The operator challenged the previous comment's disposition directly: was I smuggling a failure
to meet acceptance criteria out as 'reduced scope moved to follow-on tickets'? Partly yes, and
the correction is recorded here rather than quietly applied.

I had built a revised description that ticked eight criteria and moved three to follow-ups. It
was never applied; it is discarded. Two things in it were wrong:

**AC8 was reworded to fit the code.** The criterion says: with no sandbox mechanism available the
run ABORTS non-zero. Full stop. The implementation's `CI` branch does NOT abort — it waives with
a warning. I had rewritten the criterion to read 'on a WORKSTATION ... aborts', which converts a
FAILED criterion into a PASSED one by narrowing its scope to wherever the code happens to
succeed. The implementation's reasoning may well be right, but that makes it a criterion to be
CHANGED BY DECISION, not a criterion that was met — and the decision is the operator's, not one I
should make silently while ticking a box.

**AC6 was going to be discharged by a follow-up ticket.** I wrote that criterion specifically to
prevent inferring the Linux result from the macOS one. Filing `silicone-warless-hornet` and then
closing this ticket anyway would be exactly the inference the criterion forbids, wearing a
tracking number.

Splitting residue into follow-ups is legitimate. It stops being legitimate when the residue IS
the criterion's point. AC6 is the proof that the enforcement works on half the platforms it
claims to cover; AC11's gap means the `HOME` protection can be silently unwired with the suite
still green.

**Disposition: this ticket stays IN PROGRESS.** `silicone-warless-hornet` and
`immolated-female-lemur` are now linked `blocks`, not merely `discovered_from`, so it cannot
close until they are resolved. `overcooked-uneasy-walleye` (doc drift) remains a non-blocking
discovery.

The five criteria that ARE met (AC3's real enforcement observation, AC4, AC5, AC7, AC9, AC10)
stand on their cited evidence and are unaffected by this correction. What changes is that I am
not claiming the ticket is done.

- 724c-b5fd-efb1-40d5 (P1) _diagnose_non_killed runs surviving mutants through mutmut run WITHOUT the sandbox - the incident's exact shape, still live on main. This ticket scoped to execute_shard()'s subprocesses and never checked for mutmut run elsewhere in the module.
- c100-c4f1-2a2b-4905 (P2) enforcement tests assert file absence with no liveness check, so they pass when the sandbox fails to launch.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Round-3 plan review corrections applied, all three blocking findings addressed:

1. AC1 venv contradiction: AC1 listed 'the venv' in the allow-list while the shipped code deliberately EXCLUDES sys.prefix (a writable venv would let a mutant drop executable code into site-packages for a later un-sandboxed phase to import). AC1 now describes the shipped allow-list and states the exclusion reason. The code was right; the criterion was wrong.

2. Incomplete subprocess enumeration: the scoping section now names _diagnose_non_killed (line 660) as a THIRD mutant-executing site that re-runs surviving mutants unsandboxed, explicitly out of scope here and tracked as 724c-b5fd-efb1-40d5.

3. AC11's unverified HOME claim: confirmed empirically before fixing. Deleting 'env = mutation_sandbox.sandbox_env(env)' from execute_shard left all 70 tests green (28 sandbox + 42 gate) because the only HOME test asserted on the mapping sandbox_env returns, never on a child. Gerrit change 2274 adds three tests: two that run a real child and assert the HOME it observes (one unsandboxed so it also covers the Linux cells where probe() returns None and every @live test skips, one through wrap()), and one call-site binding test tying both sandbox-wrapped _run calls to the hardened env.

All three proven RED by real mutation, not asserted: deleting the sandbox_env call fails the binding test; pointing HOMELESS at an existing path fails both child tests; passing a wrapped subprocess the unhardened env fails the binding test. 73 tests green, make lint and make typecheck clean.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Round-4 plan review BLOCK addressed. Finding: the plan claimed a fail-closed macOS posture, but probe() detected sandbox-exec by PATH alone while verifying bwrap functionally — the exact asymmetry the probe's own docstring argues against, three lines above the check. Since sandbox-exec is Apple-deprecated, a non-enforcing stub would satisfy shutil.which, exit 0, and run every mutation effectively UNSANDBOXED on macOS (the platform the incident happened on) with no abort.

Gerrit change 2276 (MERGED) adds _seatbelt_works(), symmetric with _bwrap_works(): it runs a real sandboxed write under a deny-all profile and requires BOTH a liveness marker on stdout AND the file's absence. Absence alone is not denial — a sandbox that failed to launch leaves the file absent too.

Proven RED by mutation: reverting to the PATH-only check fails the stub-detection test; keying on exit status instead of observed denial fails it; dropping the liveness half fails the never-launched test; removing shlex.quote on the probe target fails the spaced-TMPDIR test. The real macOS sandbox-exec still probes true, so the working path is unchanged.

Three defects were caught during this change and fixed before landing: (1) the pre-existing probe-order test stubbed only shutil.which and would have FAILED on Linux, where /usr/bin/sandbox-exec does not exist — reproduced locally as 'assert None == seatbelt'; (2) the return-True branch had no non-@live coverage, so it ran on no Linux gate cell; (3) the probe interpolated its target into /bin/sh -c unquoted, so a TMPDIR containing a space would fail the redirect for a non-sandbox reason and report a denial that never happened.

One CI cell (ubuntu py3.11) failed environmentally — a Gerrit fetch timeout in the checkout step at 29s, no test executed — while py3.12, py3.13 and macOS passed on identical code. Rechecked with that reasoning recorded on the change; the rerun was green.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`scripts/mutation_gate.py` isolates the **source tree** (`git archive` into a temp dir)
but not **runtime effects**. On 2026-08-26 a mutation removed a guard from a shell
script that performs real deletion, a test exec'd it with an empty path variable, and
the glob expanded to `rm -rf /*`, destroying `/opt/homebrew` and every Homebrew app in
`/Applications` on a contributor workstation. Only a 60-second timeout stopped it,
`/Users` still ahead of it in the target list.

No mutation tool helps: cargo-mutants, mutmut, StrykerJS, PIT and mull isolate the
source tree, but **none isolates runtime effects** (see
https://mutants.rs/cautions.html). And because the harness string-substitutes the
artifact under test, any guard **inside** it is mutable — only an outer layer holds.

Scope is the **OS sandbox only**; the static lint gate split to
`6818-615f-555e-4bb9` (G5). POSIX only — `pyproject.toml` classifies the project
`POSIX` + `MacOS`, and the CI matrix is `[ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]`; Windows is
unsupported and out of scope.

## Which subprocess matters

Of the four subprocesses `execute_shard()` spawns via `_run()`, only the baseline
`pytest` and `mutmut run` execute shard test code; `mutmut results` and `show` are
reporting-only. The incident ran under `mutmut run`, which executes the *mutated* code,
so sandboxing only the baseline would leave the causal path exposed. A THIRD
mutant-executing site sits outside this function — `_diagnose_non_killed` re-runs
surviving mutants unsandboxed — out of scope, tracked as `724c-b5fd`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both shard-test-executing subprocesses in `execute_shard()` — the baseline
      `pytest` (579) **and** the `mutmut run` mutant test-run (583) — are wrapped in an
      OS-enforced sandbox denying writes outside an explicit allow-list. The venv is
      deliberately EXCLUDED from it, so a mutant cannot drop executable code into
      site-packages for a later un-sandboxed phase to import. Verified by
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py`.
- [x] The enforcement test trips the deny under **`mutmut run`** specifically, not only
      under the baseline `pytest`, since `mutmut run` is the path the incident took.
- [x] The sandbox demonstrably DENIES: a probe writing outside the allow-list exits
      non-zero and the file is absent afterward; the same probe inside the allow-list
      succeeds. Asserting wrapper argv alone does not satisfy this — the test observes
      enforcement, not construction.
- [x] macOS uses Seatbelt `sandbox-exec` with a generated `(allow default)` +
      `(deny file-write*)` + allow-list profile, reproducing the three probes measured
      on this host (macOS 26.5.2): a write outside DENIED and the file absent, a write
      inside succeeded, and `rm -rf <protected>/*` — the incident's shape — DENIED with
      the target surviving. `sandbox-exec` is Apple-deprecated, so this is a
      load-bearing external capability; see the probe criterion below. Verified by
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py` on macOS.
- [x] Linux uses `bwrap`, probed at runtime, and fails closed without it. No `unshare`
      fallback: `unshare --map-root-user --mount` denies no writes without a read-only
      remount. Verified by a test asserting the probe selects `bwrap` when present and
      returns "unavailable" when absent.
- [x] The Linux write-deny is proven **on Linux**, not inferred from macOS: the three
      probes were measured by hand in a `ubuntu:24.04` container (outside DENIED, inside
      succeeded, `rm -rf <protected>/*` DENIED with the target surviving). It is NOT
      proven by a green `ubuntu-latest` leg — those runners deny unprivileged user
      namespaces (see below), so the tests SKIP and a green leg proves nothing. That
      gating gap is tracked as `0d22-f664-77e1-495f`.
- [x] The sandbox wrapper preserves the existing `mutmut run --max-children 1`
      concurrency contract asserted at `tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py:948`.
- [x] With no sandbox mechanism available the run ABORTS non-zero with a message naming
      `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED`. Verified by a test stubbing the mechanism
      absent and asserting that literal appears in stderr.
- [x] `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED=1` waives the sandbox and logs at WARNING; a
      silent unsandboxed fallback is rejected. Verified by asserting the WARNING record
      names the same literal.
- [x] Enforcement is an OS facility invoked in-process, never a CI-provider feature, and
      works from a developer laptop with no CI involved (`project.portability`).
- [x] `HOME` is set to a non-existent path for both sandboxed subprocesses so adjacent
      home-directory writes fail loudly. Verified by RUNNING a child and asserting the
      `HOME` it observes (unsandboxed, and through `wrap()`), plus a binding test tying
      both wrapped `_run` calls to the hardened env — each proven RED. Asserting only
      the mapping `sandbox_env` returns is insufficient: with that alone, deleting the
      call left all 70 tests green.
- [x] `probe()` verifies BOTH mechanisms FUNCTIONALLY, never by `shutil.which`.
      Presence is not capability: this repo's runners ship bubblewrap but deny
      unprivileged user namespaces, and deprecated `sandbox-exec` could ship as a
      non-enforcing stub — either reports available then fails to enforce, the flaw that
      disqualified `unshare`. `_seatbelt_works` requires an observed DENIAL plus a
      liveness marker: absence alone is also what a failed launch looks like.
      Verified by `test_bwrap_present_but_unable_to_namespace_is_not_offered` and
      `test_seatbelt_present_but_not_enforcing_is_not_offered`, each proven RED.
- [x] On a CI runner (`CI` truthy) with no mechanism the gate proceeds UNSANDBOXED with
      a WARNING; on a workstation it still ABORTS — a runner is already the disposable
      environment the sandbox substitutes for. Keyed on the cross-provider `CI`
      convention, naming no provider (`project.portability`). Verified by
      `test_ci_runner_proceeds_unsandboxed_with_a_warning` and
      `test_workstation_still_aborts_when_no_sandbox`.
- [x] Bubblewrap is installed on the Linux CI lanes (`_build-and-test.yml`,
      `_mutation.yml`) so `bwrap` EXISTS there; macOS needs none. That makes the
      mechanism present, NOT enforcement verified — those runners still deny
      unprivileged user namespaces, so `probe()` returns None and the tests skip.
      Closing that gap is `0d22-f664`.
- [x] A usable sandbox is used even on CI — `CI` is a fallback for the ABSENCE of a
      mechanism, never a licence to skip a working one. Verified by
      `test_a_working_sandbox_is_used_even_on_ci`.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py` — enforcement under the baseline and
  `mutmut run`, both capability probes, fail-closed abort, opt-out, and `HOME`.
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py` — still green, including the
  `--max-children 1` concurrency contract the wrapper must preserve.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `check_complexity_baseline.py --check`.

## Definition of Done

- Every acceptance criterion above is checked by the command it names.
- The sandbox logic lands in its own module: `mutation_gate.py` is **762 LOC against the
  800 hard cap**, so it cannot absorb this inline.
- An operator note documents `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED` and its risk.


## Notes

Filed from the 2026-08-26 incident; two unrelated leaks found that day are tracked as
`a37c-d55c` and `f3d9-ecd8`. Plan review caught seven real defects, all corrected
above: `mutmut run` scoping (G6), the unnamed opt-out variable (E2), the unverified
`unshare` claim (T1/T3), AC6's false claim that a green `ubuntu-latest` leg proves
Linux enforcement, AC1's venv contradiction, AC11's unverified `HOME` claim, and the
PATH-only Seatbelt probe. Four follow-ups link `discovered_from` this ticket.
